not a fixable-in-place finding: the job is DORMANT by design (`if: vars.PUSH_EMAIL_ENABLED == 'true'`, and run history shows it skipping), it is estate-managed template content re-placed by the farm sweep, and it is the only workflow here that touches real credentials (SMTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS). RE001's suggested control, step-security/harden-runner, is used by ZERO of the estate's reusable workflows, so adopting it in one dormant caller would add a third-party dependency the estate does not run anywhere else. Discharge condition: estate-wide adoption of harden-runner (then add it here as the job's first step), or a dormancy carve-out upstream for a job whose `if:` is false in the repository's current configuration. Upstream request filed as hyperpolymath/standards#1141.

`secrets: inherit` forwards the CALLER's secret scope to mirror-reusable.yml; that reusable reads seven SSH keys (BITBUCKET_/CODEBERG_/SOURCEHUT_/DISROOT_/GITEA_/GITLAB_SSH_KEY, RADICLE_KEY) and declares none of them. Discharge condition: an upstream change to hyperpolymath/standards giving this reusable an `on.workflow_call.secrets` block. Until the reusable declares its secrets, explicit per-name forwarding is not possible at all: GitHub's reusable-workflow docs state that a named secret is passed under `secrets:` from the caller, and the note on `secrets: inherit` says referencing an UNDECLARED secret works only for inherit. So the choice here is 'hand over every secret in scope' or 'break the call' — and the estate already has the two acknowledgements this one belongs beside. Do NOT remediate this by adding a declaration to a caller copy of the reusable: the reusable is pinned by SHA and lives upstream.  Upstream request filed as hyperpolymath/standards#1141.
